surface: App Store product page, 'What's New' box under the version number; the first two or three lines show before 'more'.
reader: A Safari user who has Undirect installed or is looking at it in the store, reading on an iPhone. Same register as that locale's 1.0.5 whatsNew and description.
says: When a page tries to take the person's click or send them somewhere they did not ask for, they now see it fail on the page itself: a short note names what was stopped, and the trick visibly breaks (an invisible layer shatters, a pop-up bursts, a link swapped under the finger snaps back). So they know the site did it, not their phone.
Undirect now also runs on iPhone and iPad with iOS 18, not only the newest iOS.
For anyone who prefers it quiet: the note and the effects each switch off, in Undirect's menu in Safari or in the app.
facts_checked: Extension/Resources/background.js: banner (page note) and effects both default on from 1.1.0
Extension/Resources/content/fx.js: shatter (invisible layer), burst (pop-up or faked click), snap (swapped link)
vocabulary: Note and effects use each locale's setting_banner / setting_effects nouns from Extension/Resources/_locales.
budget: 4000 characters enforced by App Store Connect; aim under about 450 (English) so it reads in one glance.
